subject: Clarification: non-training guarantee & EU data retention/deletion
messages:

Cc: Legal Ops <legalops@finovate.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 08:12:00 +0100
Subject: Question: will Redwood use our data to train models? Data residency & deletion specifics for EU deployment

Hi Kimberly,

Quick question from our security/legal review: for our planned EU-hosted deployment, can you confirm whether Redwood will ever use Finovate Bank request/response content to further train or fine-tune model weights? We need explicit wording for the contract that states whether customer content may be used for model training or research.

Separately, please detail the default retention windows for request logs, message bodies, and cached KV layers, and describe the deletion process (how quickly data can be erased upon request and what audit evidence you can provide). We also want to understand differences (if any) between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Thanks — Emma
Emma Halvorsen
Senior Counsel, Finovate Bank
emma.halvorsen@finovate.com
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Halvorsen <emma.halvorsen@finovate.com>
Cc: Legal Ops <legalops@finovate.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 09:20:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Question: will Redwood use our data to train models? Data residency & deletion specifics for EU deployment

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear list of asks. Below is a concise, customer-facing Q&A you can use in the contract appendix. I also attached a one-page EU summary and our retention table. If you want slightly different phrasing for the SLA, tell me and we can sync with Legal.

— Q: Will Redwood use customer content to train or improve model weights?
A: No. Redwood does not use customer-provided request or response content to train, fine-tune, or improve model weights. For Hosted and Dedicated customers, customer content is segregated and is not incorporated into our training datasets or model updates. In Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments customer data remains under the customer's control and never leaves the environment unless explicitly exported by the customer.

— Q: Do you collect any telemetry that could include customer inputs?
A: We collect limited operational telemetry (latency, errors, aggregate token counts) for platform reliability and product-quality work. This telemetry is aggregated and does not contain customer message bodies. Customers can opt-out of non-essential telemetry in Dedicated and Private deployments; hosted customers should contact their account team for options.

— Q: What are the default retention windows?
A: Default hosted retention: request/response bodies are retained for 30 days; system logs (routing, errors, latency) retained for 90 days; KV/prefix caches are ephemeral and persisted only for active sessions (no long-term storage by default). Dedicated contracts can configure retention (e.g., 7/30/90 day options) as part of the reserved capacity agreement. Private deployments: retention is controlled by the customer (we provide guidance and scripts for lifecycle policies). See attached retention-table-eu.csv for a matrix.

— Q: How does deletion work and how fast can you erase data?
A: For hosted customers, we support an API-driven erase: upon authenticated request we mark data for deletion and remove it from primary serving stores within 24 hours; complete removal from backups and long-term object stores is typically within 30 days due to backup retention windows (we provide an attestation when the process completes). For Dedicated, deletion SLAs are contract-configurable and can be accelerated with emergency deletion add-ons. Private deployments are under customer control; we provide deletion runbooks and automation to remove data immediately.

— Q: Audit evidence & certifications
A: We can provide logs of deletion operations (time-stamped job IDs), SOC 2 Type II report excerpts, and a data-handling summary for EU deployments. For customers who require stronger controls, Dedicated and Private deployments support KMS/HSM keying and customer-managed encryption keys.

If you want me to reword any of the bullets for legal precision (e.g., replace 'we do not use' with 'we do not use to improve model weights'), happy to update.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Security & Compliance (Sales Enablement)
Redwood Inference

Hi Emma — looping back with the requested contractual wording and implementation details. Per internal review the contract-friendly phrasing is: 'Redwood will not use Customer Content to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve the weights of any models.'

Summary of operational controls (high level):
- Hosted (EU region): Customer Content is stored in EU-only tenancy, request/response bodies retained 30 days by default, deletions via API remove serving copies within 24 hours and complete removal from backups within 30 days (attestation provided).
- Dedicated: Isolated GPU pools and storage; retention windows are configurable; deletion SLAs are contractually agreed.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): Customer data never leaves customer network unless exported by the customer; deletion is controlled by customer ops.

We have attached the EU summary and retention matrix for your legal team. If you'd like a short 30-minute call to walk through the deletion attestation and to capture a DocuSign appendix, I'm available tomorrow morning.

Best regards,
Kimberly Park
